newsitem.title: USA: TWA sees long way to go on BA-AMR deal.
newsitem.headline: TWA sees long way to go on BA-AMR deal.

text.p: Trans World Airlines Inc said there is a long way to go to bring meaningful competition to United Kingdom and United States airline routes, if an alliance between American Airlines and British Airways Plc is approved.

On Friday, British authorities proposed conditions on an alliance between the two carriers, including the divestiture of a few airport slots and British Airways to remove a provision that blocks USAir Group Inc from competing on transatlantic routes.

TWA said the proposals for the sale of the slots held by British Airways and AMR Corp's American Airlines will not create meaningful competition and would not justify antitrust immunity to the alliance.
Also, TWA said American Airlines and British Airways should not be entitled to receive windfall profits from the sales of the airport slots.
A three-year ramp up of competition would place new entrants at a disadvantage in the markets that the proposed alliance would serve, TWA said.
